intro: “So” and “such” make an adjective or a noun stronger: “It was so hot!”, “It was such a hot day!”. They also express a result with “that”: “so tired that I fell asleep”. The rule is simple, but the two words are often confused.
objectifs: Use so + adjective / adverb and such (a / an) + (adjective) + noun.
Choose between so many / so much / so few / so little and such a lot of.
Express a result with so … that and such … that.
Tell so / such apart from very and avoid “so a” or “such beautiful”.

texte: “So” goes before an adjective on its own (with no noun after it) or before an adverb. It is more expressive than “very”: it often shows an emotion or reaction (surprise, admiration, annoyance).
The difference from very: “very” just gives information (“The film was very long”); “so” adds emotion or leads to a result (“The film was so long! I nearly fell asleep”).
exemples: The view from Mount Cameroon is so beautiful!
You speak so quickly — I can't follow you.

texte: “Such” goes before a noun phrase. With a singular countable noun, put “a / an” AFTER such: such a + (adjective) + noun. With a plural or uncountable noun, there is no article: such + (adjective) + noun.
Remember: “so + adjective” when the adjective is alone; “such + noun” as soon as there is a noun.

lignes: It was such a hot day.

sections.titre: So many, so much, such a lot of
texte: Before a quantity, use so + many / much / few / little: so many people (countable), so much traffic (uncountable), so few chairs, so little time.
“Such a lot of” is the informal equivalent for both kinds of noun: such a lot of work, such a lot of problems. Don't say “such many” or “so a lot of”.
exemples: There were so many people at the concert in Abidjan!
I have so much work this week.
We had such a lot of fun at the wedding.

texte: Add “that” + a clause to show the result. In speech, “that” is often left out: “I was so tired I fell asleep on the bus.”
The same patterns apply: so + adjective / adverb / quantity + that; such (a) + noun + that.
exemples: The exam was so difficult that half the class failed.
It was such a good film that I watched it twice.
She drove so fast that she got a fine.
There was so much noise that we couldn't talk.

texte: “So” is very common in speech, especially for emotions: “I'm so sorry”, “Thank you so much”, “It's so nice to see you”. In formal writing, people often prefer extremely, very, particularly.
“Such” can also mean “of this kind, like that”: “I've never seen such a thing”; “such as” = “for example, like”: “fruit such as mangoes and papayas”.
In a question you can say “Why are you so angry?”; for an exclamation you can also use “how”: “How beautiful!” = “It's so beautiful!”.
exemples: Thank you so much for your help.
The shop sells tropical fruit such as mangoes and pineapples.

formule: so + adjective / adverb · such (a / an) + (adjective) + noun · so many / much + noun · … (that) + result
prononciation: “so” is often lengthened and stressed for emotion: It was SOOO good! /səʊ/ (UK).
“such” is /sʌtʃ/: a short u as in “cup”, and /tʃ/ at the end as in “match”.
In “such a”, the words link: /ˈsʌtʃ ə/, almost “sutcha”.
In “so … that”, “that” is weak: /ðət/; the stress is on so and the adjective: so TIRED that…
erreurs: It was so a beautiful day.
It was such a beautiful day.
With a noun: such a, not so a.
It was a such good idea.
It was such a good idea.
I was so tired as I fell asleep.
I was so tired (that) I fell asleep.
The result is introduced by that (or nothing).
We had such a good weather.

dialogue.contexte: Kevin is back from a weekend at the Montreal jazz festival and tells his colleague Aïcha about it.
lignes: So, how was the jazz festival?
Amazing! There were so many people that we could hardly move.
It was such good music. The last band was so talented that everyone was dancing.
Lucky you! Was the weather OK?
We had such a hot weekend — 32 degrees! And the concerts finished so late.
such a + adjective + noun; so + adverb.
I am! I had such a lot of fun, but I need a holiday after my holiday!

mots: very (with emotion); to such a degree
It was such a long trip.
very (before a noun phrase); of this kind
with a natural ability to do something well
I was so exhausted that I slept for ten hours.
We could hardly hear each other.
He got a fine for driving so fast.
money you pay as a punishment
It was such a delicious meal.
I love fruit such as mangoes.

exercices.consigne: Complete with so or such (a / an if needed).
items: The soup is ___ hot that I can't eat it.
We had ___ bad luck on our trip.

exercices.titre: 2. So many, so much, such a lot of
exercices.consigne: Complete with so many, so much or such a lot of (sometimes two answers).
items: so much / such a lot of
so many / such a lot of
so much / such a lot of
There were ___ mistakes in the report.
so many / such a lot of

exercices.consigne: Join the two sentences with so … that or such … that.
items: The film was boring. I fell asleep.
The film was so boring that I fell asleep.
It was a long queue. We left.
It was such a long queue that we left.
She was nervous. She couldn't speak.
She was so nervous that she couldn't speak.
They are good friends. They talk every day.
They are such good friends that they talk every day.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: It was so a nice evening.
It was such a nice evening.
We had such a terrible weather.

exercices.consigne: Rewrite with the word in brackets. Keep the same meaning.
items: I was very tired, so I went home early. (so … that)
I was so tired that I went home early.
There was a lot of noise — too much! (so much)

exercices.consigne: Describe a memorable event (party, trip, concert, match) in five sentences with so, such and at least two results with that.
items: Last year I went to my cousin's wedding in Bafoussam. It was such a big wedding — there were more than 500 guests! The food was so delicious that I ate three plates. The music was so loud that I couldn't hear my phone. It was such a wonderful day.

a_retenir: so + adjective / adverb alone (so hot, so quickly).
such + (a / an) + (adjective) + noun (such a hot day, such kind people, such good weather).
so many / so much / so few / so little + noun; such a lot of + noun.
Never “so a” or “a such”; no a with uncountable nouns (such good weather).
